sources.title: BBMP Revenue Department — Khatha services FAQ (document rejection guidance)
sources.publisher: Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike, Revenue Department
sources.notes: Official Revenue Department FAQ page. It states that uploading incomplete or incorrect documents can lead to rejection and describes a six-step Khatha-service sequence. The page is legacy/undated and does not establish current e-Aasthi validation or a reapplication procedure.

sources.title: e-Aasthi — Upload EC Document
sources.publisher: Bengaluru City Corporations / Government of Karnataka
sources.notes: Current public portal observation. The route exposes a PropertyId/ePID lookup and EC upload. It states that an application will not be processed when the registered-deed number is not in the submitted EC, and directs a user unable to fetch EC details to contact the respective ARO. No identifier, file, or submission was used.

sources.title: BBMP Property Tax Assessment, Recovery and Management Rules, 2024 — Form 24 e-Khata Order
sources.publisher: Government of Karnataka / Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike
sources.notes: Official Gazette/rules PDF. Form 24 states that a Khatha transfer is subject to cancellation under section 150 of the BBMP Act if submitted documents are found fraudulent or a dispute arises. This is a conditional order-template safeguard, not a property-specific cancellation or live portal outcome.

claims.text: The BBMP Revenue Department FAQ states that uploading incomplete or incorrect documents can lead to rejection of a Khatha-service application.
claims.notes: The official page is legacy/undated and does not say how a current e-Aasthi rejection is displayed or whether reapplication is allowed.

claims.text: Form 24 in the BBMP Property Tax Assessment, Recovery and Management Rules, 2024 makes a Khatha transfer subject to cancellation under section 150 of the BBMP Act if the submitted documents are found fraudulent or a dispute arises.
claims.notes: This is the condition printed in the official Form 24 template; it does not establish that a particular transfer was cancelled or disclose the live review route.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi Upload EC Document route says an application will not be processed when the registered-deed number is not present in the submitted Encumbrance Certificate.
claims.notes: Current public instruction observed 2026-08-30. No property identifier, EC, or application was supplied, so no case-specific rejection was observed.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi Upload EC Document route directs a user who is unable to fetch EC details to contact the respective Assistant Revenue Officer.
claims.notes: This is a published contact handoff only; it does not establish ARO response time, evidence requirements, or resolution.

claims.text: The public eKhata Application Status view displays No Data Available when no result row is present; this does not diagnose an invalid EPID or an ownership state.
claims.notes: The blank public status view was inspected without entering an EPID. The message is a non-specific empty-result state, not an EPID validation error. The source record is reused from the existing ledger.

claims.text: After checking the public e-Aasthi property search, eKhata application-status, and Upload EC routes, no official public procedure was found that diagnoses an unresolved or incorrect EPID or provides an EPID-specific correction or recovery path for a clean-sale case.
claims.notes: The pass checked the public search controls, the blank status result, and the public PropertyId/EC route without entering an identifier. The visible generic helpline and missing-property route are not treated as EPID-specific correction procedures.
